chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not kill a man by his own hand ever, except for one man, Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, may God curse him, and he struck Ibn Abi Khalaf and he died after that.

key_terms.اِبْنَ أَبِي خَلَفٍ: Ibn Abi Khalaf, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.عُقْبَةَ بْنِ أَبِي مُعَيْطٍ: Uqba ibn Abi Muayt, a specific companion known for persecuting Muslims

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad kill anyone with his own hand according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* emphasizes the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) personal restraint in execution, citing Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt as the sole exception due to his specific treachery and refusal to accept Islam despite clear signs. The mention of Ibn Abi Khalaf illustrates a distinct category of death by wound rather than direct execution, reflecting the nuanced Shia understanding of judicial versus personal retribution in early Islamic history.
